note: Usable width between the shelf brackets.

instrument: Tape measure, shelf to the cupboard above
note: Measured with the lid's swing in mind, not just the closed height.
The 41 mm axis is the one the reed switch sits against, which is why the sensor has to stand on its edge rather than lie flat.
11 mm is the depth into the wall once the sensor is stood on edge. This is what costs 13.8 mm of interior depth at the front.

instrument: Visual inspection against the vendor manual
note: The manual says to align the marker lines on body and magnet. Laying the sensor flat, which is the obvious thing to do, puts the magnet off-axis.

instrument: Printed spacer stack between magnet and sensor, watching the Zigbee state change in the coordinator log
note: Closed by watching the reported state CHANGE at a known gap, not by reading a number off a page. A steady 'closed' reading proves nothing - the sensor reports closed when it is unpowered too.

instrument: Zigbee LQI logged from the coordinator, sensor inside the closed printed box on the actual shelf
note: Tested in place, through the real walls, in plain PLA. Not on the desk next to the coordinator.
